Department of Interior June 28, 1972
Page Eight
C. Bureau of Land Management
As pointed out in the Draft Statement, BLM is responsible for the management of approximately 452 million acres of public land. In general, the BLM lands do not possess the unique scenic, natural, historic or archeological characteristics present in the NPS lands nor do they generally function as important wildlife conservation centers as is the case with the BSFW lands. Public use of BLM lands is generally low density in nature and BLM has limited personnel available for the purpose of enforcing any regulation of ORRV use. Based on these factors. the historical BLM policy with respect to ORRV use has been to permit such use in all areas except those which are closed to such use for a specific reason. The Department's proposed implementation of the Executive Order would apparently reverse this policy and would provide for the confining of ORRV use to areas and trails designated as open to such use. Even in such open areas, ORRV use would be subject to certain controls.
while the Association does not disagree with the goal of imposing reasonable restrictions on ORRV use in any area of the BLM lands, it does strongly disagree with the Department's apparent intention to reverse BLM's historical approach with respect to the classification of lands.
